Gold/silver diverged from the equity rally on real yields, not risk-off: GLD -1.13%, miners -1 to -1.5% (GDX, SILJ, SLVP, NEM, PAAS, AG, HL) even as SLV held up (+0.37%) on industrial/AI-power demand; intraday Thu-Asia quotes show gold briefly under $4,000 and silver under $52 -- levels to watch at the SGX/HKEX-adjacent open, not confirmed closes.

China's rare-earth export-control truce expired Nov 10 with no formal renewal confirmed -- the live catalyst behind this week's rare-earth-basket strength (MP, Lynas, Energy Fuels, USAR all firm); watch for a MOFCOM notice in the coming days.
HK tech mixed: Tencent -1.96%, Xiaomi -1.63%, but SMIC +3.73% on a chip-self-sufficiency read-through as the Nvidia 'spy scandal' accelerates new congressional chip-export-control bills.

Singapore banks split (OCBC beat, DBS/UOB missed) even as the STI firmed; Korea's foreign-buying streak extended to 2 days (Nov 10-11) but retail flipped to selling Nov 11 -- the first session foreign buying and retail selling have coincided, a tentative stabilization tell.
